question: Refer to the exhibit. SVR-A in EPG-A/BD-A fails to reach SVR-B in EPG-B/BD-B. Which two conditions should be verified to analyze the traffic between the two EPGs? (Choose two.)
context: Topology: two ACI spine switches connect to Node-110, Node-111, Node-112. Node-110 has BD-A/EPG-A -> SVR-A. Node-112 has BD-B/EPG-B -> SVR-B. Both in VRF-1.
imageNote: Diagram: two ACI spine switches connect to leaf Node-110, Node-111, and Node-112 (all in VRF-1). Node-110 hosts BD-A/EPG-A leading to SVR-A; Node-112 hosts BD-B/EPG-B leading to SVR-B.
options: A contract exists between EPG-A and EPG-B and allows the traffic.
The bridge domain for EPG-B floods ARP packets.
EPG-A and EPG-B are excluded from the preferred group.
Limit Endpoint Learning is disabled on the bridge domain for EPG-B.
SVR-B is learned as an endpoint in EPG-B from Node-112.
theory: Two independent conditions must both be verified when SVR-A cannot reach SVR-B across EPGs in ACI: first, a contract must exist between EPG-A and EPG-B that explicitly permits the required traffic, since ACI denies inter-EPG traffic by default in the absence of a contract; second, the destination endpoint SVR-B must actually be learned by the fabric under EPG-B on the correct leaf (Node-112), since ACI's policy enforcement and forwarding both depend on accurate endpoint learning - a missing contract or an unlearned endpoint will independently break connectivity even if the other condition is satisfied. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Cisco ACI Contracts and endpoint learning)
